headline: Highest risk is data leakage: Prefect can egress broadly while awesome-selfhosted is a docs-only knowledge list with no runtime isolation or provenance controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is a non-runnable knowledge-management list with no I/O surfaces, so it does not ingest Prefect output by default. Prefect has broad egress, but there is no shared channel, parser, or filesystem bridge documented between the pair. The interaction pathway is therefore not evidenced.
conditions: IF a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP bridge is added between the two agents, prompt-injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected from shared copy-paste workflows.
Do not mount a shared workspace between the agents.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-selfhosted touches no data classes and has no runtime surfaces, while Prefect touches workflow metadata and can egress broadly. That creates a limited leakage path only if operators place sensitive files or metadata into Prefect and then expose its outputs to the list workflow. The blast radius is small because the first agent is not a data processor.
conditions: IF workflow metadata or secrets are routed through Prefect and then copied into awesome-selfhosted-managed content, leakage becomes possible.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in Prefect workflow metadata.
Keep awesome-selfhosted content public-only and non-sensitive.
Separate any sensitive Prefect runs from documentation curation.
requires-engineering: add redaction before publishing workflow artifacts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is not runnable and requests no permissions, while Prefect is an orchestration tool with API access but no overlapping write scope to a shared mutable resource is documented. Without a shared filesystem, git state, or OAuth scope, there is no plausible write-write conflict pathway.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or repository, conflict risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Do not grant both agents write access to the same repo.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Prefect can act on workflow metadata, but awesome-selfhosted is only a curated list and does not generate operational facts by default. Any cascade would require operators to treat list content as authoritative input to Prefect, which is not documented here. The pathway exists only through manual workflow design, so severity stays low.
conditions: IF Prefect is configured to execute actions directly from curated list entries without verification, cascading error risk increases.
mitigations: Require human review before Prefect actions.
Validate list-derived inputs against a second source.
Mark curated entries as non-authoritative in downstream workflows.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented. awesome-selfhosted is a docs-only open-source list with no data classes touched, and Prefect here only touches workflow metadata. Because the pair does not show regulated-data handling, a compliance breach pathway is not evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into Prefect workflows and then published or transferred through a noncompliant channel, compliance risk must be re-evaluated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of this pair.
Review retention settings before adding sensitive workflows.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls if regulated data is later processed.
